description: Search recipes on BBC Good Food and return a listing. Narrow it with 'diet', 'cuisine', 'meal_type', 'difficulty' or a bound such as 'max_total_minutes'; call list_filters first for the values each one takes, since the site answers a value it does not know with a count of zero. The site ranks rather than filters: it answers a term it holds nothing for with rows all the same, so read the titles rather than trusting the count. Each row carries the page to read the recipe on.

exclude_premium.description: Drop the rows that sit behind the site's subscription. The site offers no such restriction, so the rows are removed from the page after it arrives: a page comes back shorter than the limit asked for, and a short page is not the end of the results.

min_rating.description: At least this many stars, 1 to 5.

query.description: A dish, an ingredient, a technique.

sort.description: How the site orders the rows. Default 'relevant'.

name: search_recipes

premium_dropped.description: Rows removed from this page for sitting behind the site's subscription.

restrictions_lifted.description: Restrictions let go of so the search could run again after the restricted one returned nothing.

result_count.description: Rows rendered, after anything unreadable was set aside.

difficulty.description: The site's own wording, such as 'Easy'.

id.description: The page's own path. Pass it to get_recipe to read the recipe.

premium.description: True when the recipe sits behind the site's subscription.

rating.description: 1 to 5. Null when the site published none.

total_minutes.description: Null when the site states no time.

url.description: The public page. Show this when citing the recipe.

rows_seen.description: Rows the site served, before anything was set aside.

total_available.description: Recipes the site says the search holds.

total_is_ceiling.description: True when the total sits on the most rows one search will serve, so it states a floor.

title: Search recipes
